Top Roofing Marketing Blogs Contractors Should Follow

The top 30 roofing marketing blogs every contractor should follow. Includes marketing tips, industry news, and growth strategies.

OnwardCraft Team Growth Strategists

You are competing against 106,000 other roofing companies for the same homeowner clicks. The contractors who win are not the ones with the biggest trucks. They are the ones who consume the right information, apply it faster, and out-market everyone else. This list of 30 roofing marketing blogs, podcasts, YouTube channels, and social media accounts is the exact resource stack that separates six-figure roofers from seven-figure operations. Whether you are trying to rank on Google Maps, run profitable Facebook ads, or build a brand that sells roofs while you sleep, every resource here has been vetted for real-world results.

Why Roofing Marketing Blogs Matter More Than Ever in 2026

The U.S. roofing contractor industry generated approximately $76.4 billion in revenue during 2025 and is projected to approach $99.8 billion by 2026, according to IBISWorld data. With over 101,000 roofing businesses operating nationwide and no single company holding more than 5 percent market share, the competitive pressure has never been higher.

Here is the reality most contractors miss: 54 percent of homeowners use online search before booking a roofing contractor, yet 70 percent of roofers are dissatisfied with their current SEO results. The gap between what contractors know about marketing and what actually works is costing them millions in lost revenue. Roofing marketing blogs bridge that gap by delivering tested strategies, real case studies, and actionable frameworks without the $5,000 agency price tag.

But not all roofing marketing blogs are equal. Many recycle generic advice that stopped working three algorithm updates ago. The 30 resources in this article are different. They are run by people who have actually built roofing companies, generated roofing leads at scale, or spent years inside the industry. Every entry includes what they cover, why it matters, and how to apply their content to your business.

The Cost of Marketing Ignorance in Roofing

Let us look at the numbers. The average roofing cost-per-click on Google Ads sits at $11.13, making it one of the most expensive home service categories. Contractors who do not understand landing page optimization, ad copy psychology, and conversion tracking routinely burn through $10,000 monthly budgets with little to show for it. Meanwhile, roofers who invest 7 to 12 percent of revenue into strategic marketing and actually know what they are doing consistently outperform competitors spending twice as much.

The roofing marketing blogs in this guide cover every channel that matters: local SEO, Google Business Profile optimization, paid advertising, email marketing, video content, social media, and reputation management. Following even five of these resources consistently will put you ahead of 90 percent of your competition.

The 12 Best Roofing Marketing Blogs for Lead Generation and Growth

These are the blogs that publish original, tested marketing strategies specifically for roofing contractors. They are not generic marketing blogs that occasionally mention roofing. They are written by people who understand storm season cash flow, insurance supplement workflows, and the difference between a retail lead and a hail damage lead.

1. Roofing Webmasters Blog — Nolen Walker

Nolen Walker founded Roofing Webmasters in 2013 after his own frustrating experiences with marketing agencies while running a home services business. His blog is the most technically deep roofing marketing resource on the internet. Walker does not publish fluff. He publishes 2,000-word guides on Google Maps ranking factors, E-E-A-T signals for roofing websites, and why most roofer blog posts generate zero traffic.

His core thesis is simple: most roofing SEO advice from generalist gurus is wrong for contractors. Walker argues that service pages with recent job photos outperform generic blog posts for local rankings. His proprietary DataPins software automates this process by pulling actual project data into website content. If you want to understand why your website is not ranking in the Map Pack, start here.

2. Hook Agency Blog — Tim Brown

Tim Brown built Hook Agency from a two-person shop into a 55-plus person agency specializing in home service contractors. His roofing marketing blog covers SEO, paid ads, website design, and lead magnets with a focus on persuasive copywriting. Brown is particularly strong on emotional benefit-driven messaging, a technique most roofing contractors ignore in favor of feature lists.

Hook Agency's case studies show real numbers: 200 percent year-over-year increases in first-page rankings, 92.98 percent increases in qualified organic leads, and $143 cost-per-conversion with Google Ads. Brown also publishes profit margin analysis for roofing companies, helping contractors understand what they can realistically afford to spend on marketing.

3. Roofer Marketing Heroes Blog — Chris Hunter

Chris Hunter has built over 1,055 roofing websites and generated more than 703,000 appointments for contractor clients. His blog, Roofer Marketing Heroes, publishes practical guides on SEO, Google Maps optimization, PPC, video marketing, and AI tools for roofers. Hunter's "Ultimate Guide to Digital Marketing for Roofers" is one of the most downloaded resources in the industry.

What sets Hunter apart is his willingness to share exact systems. He has published the complete framework that grew one roofing company from $350,000 to $3 million in two years. That level of transparency is rare in contractor marketing.

4. Local Roofing SEO Agency Blog

This blog focuses exclusively on local search domination for roofing contractors. Their 2026 digital marketing guide covers Google Business Profile optimization, citation building, review generation, and local content strategies. The blog is particularly valuable for contractors in competitive markets like Dallas, Houston, and Phoenix who need to outrank established competitors.

5. BuildRight Digital Blog

BuildRight Digital publishes actionable roofing marketing ideas with a strong emphasis on SEO and content marketing. Their 2026 guide covers 17 specific marketing tactics, from storm damage content strategies to direct mail campaigns that still work in older neighborhoods. The blog is written for contractors who want to execute marketing themselves rather than outsource everything.

6. Red Brick Web Blog

Red Brick Web specializes in marketing strategies for roofing companies, with a focus on storm damage marketing and review generation. Their blog breaks down how to create cost-comparison content that attracts high-intent homeowners in the research phase. This is critical because homeowners who search "how much does a roof replacement cost" are typically 30 to 60 days from making a purchase decision.

7. AMRA and Elma Blog

AMRA and Elma publish data-driven roofing marketing statistics and industry trend reports. Their 2026 statistics compilation is one of the most cited resources in roofing marketing circles. If you need current data on cost-per-click trends, homeowner behavior shifts, or marketing budget benchmarks, this is your source.

8. Roofing Business Partner Blog — Adam Sand

Adam Sand runs Roofing Business Partner and is a certified SumoQuote implementation partner. His blog and podcast content focus on building marketing and sales funnels that contractors actually own, rather than depending on lead brokers. Sand's five key tips for roofing growth include nailing service-market fit, tracking the right KPIs, delivering a five-minute customer experience, and avoiding the "CRM doom loop" that paralyzes so many contractors.

9. Roofing Success Blog — Jim Ahlin

Jim Ahlin co-founded Roofer Marketers and co-authored "Internet Marketing For Roofing Contractors: How to Triple Your Sales." While his primary platform is the Roofing Success Podcast, the accompanying blog publishes detailed show notes, marketing frameworks, and guest insights from industry leaders. Recent topics include speed-to-lead optimization and 2025 year-end lessons that every contractor should apply in 2026.

10. Minyona Blog — Michael Mignogna

Michael Mignogna runs Minyona, a Baltimore-based digital marketing agency for roofing contractors. His Scrappy Wins podcast and blog focus on marketing that actually works for home service providers. Mignogna also runs the Minyona Contractor Systems community on Skool, where paying members get exclusive training on converting leads into deals, including selling roofs through Facebook.

11. ServiceTitan Roofing Blog

ServiceTitan is the dominant software platform for home service contractors, and their roofing blog reflects that scale. They publish comprehensive guides on roofing industry trends, business growth strategies, and marketing efficiency. Their 2026 market report surveyed over 1,000 roofing companies and found that 75 percent expect revenue growth, yet only 16 percent follow up with homeowners same-day for unsold estimates. That gap is a massive marketing opportunity.

12. AccuLynx Blog

AccuLynx is the leading CRM for roofing contractors, and their blog publishes 92 roofing marketing ideas alongside operational advice. While AccuLynx is primarily a sales and project management tool, their marketing content covers lead intelligence, automation workflows, and photo-based marketing strategies that help contractors turn project documentation into sales assets.

The 8 Essential Roofing Industry Publications for Market Intelligence

Marketing without industry context is like roofing without knowing the pitch. These publications keep you informed about material costs, labor shortages, insurance industry shifts, and regulatory changes that directly impact your marketing messaging.

1. Roofing Contractor Magazine

Roofing Contractor Magazine is the premier resource for roofing professionals and the official publication of the International Roofing Expo. Published by BNP Media, it covers business management, new products, safety regulations, and insurance developments. The magazine produces the annual Top 100 and Top 150 Roofing Contractors rankings, which offer valuable competitive intelligence.

For marketing purposes, Roofing Contractor Magazine is essential because it reveals where the industry is heading. When the magazine covers new building codes or insurance carrier policy changes, smart contractors adjust their marketing messaging immediately. For example, when insurance carriers began shortening acceptable roof ages to 15 to 20 years, contractors who updated their website content and ad copy to address this trend captured a wave of anxious homeowners.

2. Professional Roofing Magazine

Professional Roofing is the official magazine of the National Roofing Contractors Association (NRCA). It covers technical research, government regulations, workforce development, and business management. The magazine is free with an NRCA membership and offers both print and digital subscriptions.

Recent coverage has included AI applications in roofing, mental health initiatives for workers, and bipartisan housing legislation that affects contractor demand. Marketing-savvy contractors use this publication to identify emerging trends before competitors, then create content around those topics to capture early search traffic.

3. NRCA Blog and Resources

The National Roofing Contractors Association publishes technical manuals, training programs, and advocacy updates. Their 2025 Roofing Manual: Steep-slope Roof Systems is the industry standard. For marketers, the NRCA's workforce and regulatory updates provide content angles that resonate with both commercial and residential audiences.

4. RoofersCoffeeShop

RoofersCoffeeShop is an award-winning online community that has served the roofing industry for over 20 years. Founded by Heidi J. Ellsworth and Vickie Sharples, it combines industry news, podcasts, forums, and classified ads. The site covers technology adoption, sustainability innovations, and association events.

What makes RoofersCoffeeShop valuable for marketing is its community-driven content. The forums reveal real contractor pain points, which become content ideas. The podcasts feature interviews with successful contractors who share what actually worked in their marketing. Their sister site, MetalCoffeeShop, extends this coverage to metal construction.

5. GAF Blog

GAF is the largest roofing manufacturer in North America, and their blog publishes product innovation updates, installation best practices, and contractor program information. While manufacturer blogs are often promotional, GAF's content provides valuable material for contractor websites. When GAF releases a new shingle line or warranty update, contractors who publish timely content about these changes capture search traffic from homeowners researching products.

6. Owens Corning Roofing Blog

Owens Corning emphasizes sustainability and material science innovation in their content. Their blog covers SureNail technology, TruDefinition color platforms, and Platinum Preferred Contractor program updates. Contractors certified with Owens Corning can leverage this content to build trust with homeowners who prioritize brand-name materials and comprehensive warranties.

7. CertainTeed Roofing Blog

CertainTeed positions itself as the premium alternative to GAF, and their blog reflects that focus. Content covers luxury shingle lines, design inspiration, and Select ShingleMaster certification requirements. For contractors targeting high-end residential markets, CertainTeed's blog provides the technical depth needed to justify premium pricing in marketing materials.

8. Atlas Roofing Asphalt Life Blog

Atlas Roofing launched Asphalt Life in 2017 as a resource for both contractors and homeowners. The blog covers business strategies, sales training, and casual lifestyle content. Atlas also provides extensive marketing resources for contractors in their Atlas Pro program, including logo usage guidelines, promotional materials, and digital tools like the Shingle Visualizer.

The 6 Roofing Podcasts That Will Change How You Think About Marketing

Podcasts are the ultimate multitasking learning tool for contractors who spend hours driving between job sites. These six shows deliver marketing insights you can implement the same day.

1. The Roof Strategist Podcast — Adam Bensman

Adam Bensman's podcast is the most followed free roofing sales training network in the industry, with millions of views across platforms. Episodes run 10 to 22 minutes and drop every Monday and Thursday. Bensman covers retail roofing sales, storm damage sales, door-to-door canvassing, and objection handling.

While primarily a sales podcast, the marketing implications are massive. Bensman teaches contractors how to craft pitches that convert, which directly informs ad copy, landing page headlines, and email subject lines. He is also the official sales training partner for Owens Corning and author of "The Roofing Sales Survival Guide."

2. Roofing Success Podcast — Jim Ahlin

Jim Ahlin interviews roofing industry leaders about digital marketing, lead generation, and business scaling. The podcast covers SEO, paid advertising, website optimization, and operational systems. Recent episodes have explored speed-to-lead strategies and year-end lessons from 2025 that contractors must apply in 2026.

3. Roofer Growth Hacks — Chris Hunter

Chris Hunter's podcast focuses on digital marketing trends, growth strategies, and expert interviews. With 23 years of online marketing experience, Hunter brings a depth of knowledge that goes beyond surface-level tips. His monthly "state of the industry" episodes help contractors understand which marketing channels are working right now versus which ones are fading.

4. Roofing SEO Podcast — Nolen Walker

Nolen Walker's podcast delivers short-form SEO education in 11 to 16 minute episodes. He covers Google Maps ranking, website content strategy, review generation, and branding. Walker's approach is refreshingly direct: he tells roofers exactly what to do, what to avoid, and why most SEO advice from generalist gurus is wrong for contractors.

5. Scrappy Wins — Michael Mignogna

Michael Mignogna's podcast is for contractors who want marketing that actually works. Episodes average 23 minutes and feature both educational content and long-form interviews with actual clients. Mignogna focuses on practical strategies for Facebook marketing, lead conversion, and building marketing systems that do not require a PhD in digital advertising.

6. Hook Better Leads — Tim Brown

Tim Brown's podcast covers marketing, sales, leadership, and mindset for roofers and contractors. Episodes explore lead generation, conversion optimization, and the psychology behind why homeowners choose one contractor over another. Brown's background in persuasive copywriting makes this podcast particularly valuable for contractors who want to improve their messaging.

Bonus: General Contractor Marketing Podcasts

Three additional podcasts deliver marketing insights that apply directly to roofing:

  • Toolbox for the Trades — ServiceTitan's podcast covering marketing, operations, and scaling for home service businesses.
  • Contractor Radio — Jim Johnson's show focusing on sales and marketing for contractors.
  • NAILED IT! The Business of Construction — Joseph Hughes covers digital marketing strategies for contractors of all trades.

The 6 YouTube Channels Every Roofing Contractor Should Subscribe To

YouTube is the second largest search engine in the world, and roofing content is exploding. These channels combine marketing education with business strategy.

1. Roofing Insights — Dmitry Lipinskiy

Dmitry Lipinskiy's Roofing Insights channel has approximately 183,000 subscribers, making it the largest roofing business channel on YouTube. Lipinskiy founded the channel in 2017 while running Storm Group Roofing, which he grew to over $5 million in annual revenue before selling.

The channel covers product reviews, industry investigations, contractor interviews, and business education. Lipinskiy is known for exposing scams and unethical practices, which builds massive trust with his audience. For contractors, Roofing Insights offers a masterclass in using controversy and investigative content to build a brand. Lipinskiy also runs Roofing Business School and the Directorii platform, which connects homeowners with vetted contractors.

2. The Roof Strategist — Adam Bensman

Adam Bensman's YouTube channel has approximately 72,000 subscribers and complements his podcast perfectly. The channel features sales role-plays, door-knocking techniques, and closing strategies. For marketing purposes, Bensman's content teaches contractors how to think like salespeople, which transforms how they write ad copy, design landing pages, and structure follow-up sequences.

3. Roofer Growth Hacks — Chris Hunter

Chris Hunter's YouTube channel extends his podcast content with visual demonstrations of marketing tactics. He covers SEO tutorials, Google Ads walkthroughs, and website reviews. Hunter's video content is particularly valuable for contractors who are visual learners and need to see exactly how to implement marketing strategies.

4. Roofing SEO Podcast — Nolen Walker

Nolen Walker's YouTube channel features video versions of his podcast episodes, plus screen recordings of SEO tools and website audits. Contractors can watch him analyze actual roofing websites, identify ranking problems, and recommend fixes. This hands-on approach makes complex SEO concepts accessible to non-technical business owners.

5. Scrappy Wins / Minyona — Michael Mignogna

Michael Mignogna's YouTube channel focuses on Facebook marketing, lead conversion, and sales strategies for roofing contractors. His content is practical and implementation-focused, with less theory and more "here is exactly what to do." For contractors spending money on Facebook ads, this channel is essential.

6. RoofersCoffeeShop

The RoofersCoffeeShop YouTube channel features industry news, technology updates, and interviews with roofing leaders. While less focused on marketing tactics than other channels, it provides the industry context that informs smart marketing decisions. Understanding where the industry is heading helps contractors position their messaging ahead of trends.

Video Marketing Best Practices for Roofing Contractors

These YouTube channels do more than educate. They model the exact video content that roofing contractors should be creating for their own marketing. Here is what the data shows:

  • 85 percent of social video is watched without sound, so captions are non-negotiable.
  • 15 to 30 second shorts for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts generate the highest engagement.
  • Before-and-after reveal videos, damage discovery clips, and time-lapse installations consistently outperform polished commercials.
  • Contractors who film on actual job sites build more trust than those using stock footage.

How to Actually Use These 30 Resources (Without Getting Overwhelmed)

Thirty resources is a lot. Here is how to consume them strategically based on your business stage and goals.

The 30-Minute Daily Routine

Successful contractors do not binge-read marketing blogs on Sunday night. They build a daily habit. Here is a framework that works:

  1. Monday: Read one article from a roofing marketing blog. Focus on implementation, not inspiration. Ask: what can I do today?
  2. Tuesday: Listen to one podcast episode during your commute. Take one note on your phone.
  3. Wednesday: Watch one YouTube video. Follow along on your own website or ad account if possible.
  4. Thursday: Review one industry publication for trends that affect your messaging.
  5. Friday: Study one social media account. Analyze what they post, when they post, and how their audience responds.
  6. Weekend: Implement one thing you learned during the week. Action beats consumption every time.

Match Resources to Your Business Stage

Not every resource is right for every contractor. Here is how to prioritize:

  • Startup (under $500K revenue): Focus on Hook Agency, BuildRight Digital, and The Roof Strategist. You need foundational marketing knowledge and low-cost tactics.
  • Growth ($500K to $2M): Add Roofing Webmasters, Roofer Marketing Heroes, and Roofing Success Podcast. You need to systematize your marketing.
  • Scale ($2M to $10M): Prioritize ServiceTitan, AccuLynx, and industry publications. You need operational efficiency and competitive intelligence.
  • Enterprise ($10M+): Follow Roofing Insights, Roofing Contractor Magazine, and NRCA resources. You need industry-level strategy and regulatory awareness.

Create Your Content Swipe File

As you consume these resources, build a swipe file. This is a simple document where you save headlines, ad copy, email subject lines, and social posts that catch your attention. When you need to write your next Facebook ad or landing page, you will have a library of proven examples to reference. The best marketers in every industry keep swipe files. There is no reason roofing contractors should not do the same.

Apply the 80/20 Rule

Twenty percent of these resources will deliver 80 percent of your value. After 30 days of following this list, identify which three to five sources give you the most actionable ideas. Double down on those. Unsubscribe from the rest. Information overload is real, and it paralyzes more contractors than ignorance does.

Track Your Marketing Experiments

Every blog post, podcast episode, and YouTube video should lead to one experiment. Create a simple spreadsheet with these columns: idea source, tactic tested, date started, cost, leads generated, cost per lead, and notes. After 90 days, you will have data on what actually works for your specific market. That data is worth more than any blog post.

Frequently Asked Questions About Roofing Marketing Blogs

What are roofing marketing blogs?

Roofing marketing blogs are online publications that publish articles, guides, and resources specifically about marketing strategies for roofing contractors. They cover topics like SEO, paid advertising, social media, website design, lead generation, and sales conversion. Unlike general marketing blogs, roofing marketing blogs understand the unique challenges of the industry, including seasonal demand, insurance claim workflows, and storm restoration cycles.

How often should roofing contractors read marketing blogs?

Contractors should spend 20 to 30 minutes daily consuming marketing content. This is more effective than binge-reading for hours once a week. A daily habit keeps you current on algorithm changes, new ad platform features, and competitor strategies. The key is to pair consumption with implementation. For every hour you spend reading, spend at least two hours executing.

Which roofing marketing blog is best for SEO?

Roofing Webmasters, run by Nolen Walker, is the most technically deep resource for roofing SEO. His blog covers Google Maps optimization, E-E-A-T signals, local search ranking factors, and content strategies that actually work for contractors. Hook Agency also publishes strong SEO content with a focus on persuasive copywriting and conversion optimization.

What is the best roofing podcast for marketing?

The Roofing Success Podcast with Jim Ahlin is the best marketing-focused show, featuring interviews with industry leaders about digital marketing, lead generation, and business scaling. For sales-specific marketing, The Roof Strategist with Adam Bensman is unmatched. For SEO, the Roofing SEO Podcast with Nolen Walker delivers the most actionable technical advice.

How much should roofing contractors spend on marketing?

Industry standards recommend 7 to 12 percent of revenue for marketing. Small contractors under $5 million should budget 7 to 8 percent. Growth-mode companies should invest 8 to 10 percent. Large regional companies often spend 10 to 12 percent. The key is not the percentage but the return on investment. A contractor spending 5 percent with a 500 percent ROI outperates one spending 15 percent at break-even.

Do roofing manufacturer blogs help with marketing?

Yes, but indirectly. Manufacturer blogs like GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, and Atlas Roofing provide product updates, warranty information, and installation guides. Smart contractors use this content to create their own educational materials. When a manufacturer releases a new product or warranty change, contractors who publish timely content about it capture search traffic from homeowners researching those products.

Can roofing contractors learn marketing from general contractor blogs?

General contractor marketing blogs like Contractor Growth Network and NAILED IT! cover principles that apply to roofing, including local SEO, paid advertising, and website optimization. However, roofing has unique elements like storm seasonality, insurance supplements, and hail damage marketing that generalist blogs rarely address. Use general blogs for foundational knowledge, but rely on roofing-specific resources for industry tactics.

What social media platform is best for roofing marketing?

Facebook generates the most leads for residential roofing, with 84 percent of roofers reporting it as their top lead source. Instagram works best for visual portfolio building and brand awareness. LinkedIn is essential for commercial roofing B2B marketing. TikTok and YouTube Shorts are emerging as legitimate lead generation channels for contractors willing to create authentic, short-form video content.

How do roofing industry publications help with marketing?

Industry publications like Roofing Contractor Magazine and Professional Roofing reveal trends before they hit the mainstream. When publications cover new building codes, insurance policy changes, or material innovations, smart contractors immediately update their website content and ad copy to address these topics. This early-mover advantage captures search traffic before competitors react.

What is the fastest way to implement what I learn from roofing marketing blogs?

The fastest implementation path is: read one tactic, test it within 48 hours, measure results for two weeks, then either scale or abandon. Most contractors fail not because they lack knowledge but because they consume endlessly without executing. Create a simple tracking spreadsheet for your marketing experiments. After 90 days, the data will tell you exactly what works in your market.

Are roofing marketing blogs worth the time investment?

Absolutely. Contractors who consistently consume and implement marketing education routinely outperform competitors who rely on intuition or outdated tactics. The roofing industry changes rapidly. Google updates its algorithm hundreds of times per year. Facebook ad costs fluctuate. Insurance carrier policies shift. Roofing marketing blogs keep you ahead of these changes without the cost of a full-time marketing director.

How do I choose which roofing marketing blogs to follow?

Start with three to five resources that match your current business stage and biggest marketing challenge. If you need more leads, follow Hook Agency and Roofer Marketing Heroes. If you need better SEO, follow Roofing Webmasters. If you need sales training, follow The Roof Strategist. After 30 days, evaluate which sources delivered the most actionable ideas and double down on those.

Can I get featured on a roofing marketing blog list like this one?

Yes. Blog lists like this one are updated annually, and editors are always looking for new resources that deliver real value. To get featured, build a consistent publishing schedule, share original insights that cannot be found elsewhere, and demonstrate real results from your strategies. If you believe your blog, podcast, or channel deserves recognition, reach out to publications with specific examples of your best content.

What is the biggest mistake roofing contractors make with marketing?

The biggest mistake is treating marketing as an expense rather than an investment. Contractors who view marketing as a necessary evil consistently underinvest, switch strategies too frequently, and abandon tactics before they have time to work. The contractors who win treat marketing like any other profit center. They track ROI, optimize based on data, and reinvest profits into scaling what works.

Your 30-Day Action Plan

Knowledge without action is entertainment. Here is exactly what to do in the next 30 days to turn this list into revenue.

Week 1: Audit your current marketing. List every channel you are using, how much you are spending, and what results you are getting. Identify the one channel with the highest ROI and the one channel that is wasting money.

Week 2: Pick three resources from this list that address your biggest weakness. Subscribe to their email lists, follow their social accounts, and listen to or read their most recent five pieces of content.

Week 3: Implement one tactic from each resource. Do not overthink it. Launch the Facebook ad. Rewrite the service page. Set up the review automation. Done beats perfect.

Week 4: Measure results. Did leads increase? Did cost per lead decrease? Did website traffic grow? Use this data to decide what to scale, what to adjust, and what to abandon.

Repeat this cycle monthly. In 12 months, you will have tested 36 marketing tactics, doubled down on the winners, and built a lead generation system that runs whether you are on a roof or on vacation.
